A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 44 readable pages including Appendices A–I. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the figures, tables, equations and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original language-model experiments on likelihood displacement, CHES-based sample selection and safety alignment in Sections 3, 5 and 6 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and their outcomes, including Table 1, Figures 2–4 and the supplementary results in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The CHES score, length-normalized variant, filtering procedure and analyzed preference-learning objectives are unchanged. No algorithm or model component is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Persona, UltraFeedback, AlpacaFarm and SORRY-Bench coverage, with unchanged tasks and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Section 5 retains normalized edit distance and last-hidden-embedding inner products as CHES comparators. Section 6 retains the same SFT-regularization and gold-preference comparisons, with unchanged appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Model configurations, training procedures, metrics, 512-sample subsets and the SORRY-Bench 85%/15% split are unchanged. Section 6.1 corrects an appendix pointer without changing any experimental setting.

E4.justification: The no-initial-SFT controls, embedding-geometry and coefficient analyses, CHES examples and refusal case studies are retained unchanged, including Appendix H.

E5.justification: The repeated-run information in Appendix I and three-run averages with minimum–maximum error bars in Figures 2–3 are unchanged. No uncertainty reporting or statistical procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the appendix tables and figures. Both versions report the same Llama-3-8B-Instruct refusal-rate decrease from 74.4% to 33.4% in Section 6.2.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theorems, propositions and proofs are unchanged. The edit to the displayed E(theta) expression in Appendix E.1 only adds a terminal period.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about catastrophic likelihood displacement, embedding geometry, CHES prediction and mitigation through data filtering.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, result interpretations and Section 8.1 limitations are unchanged, including qualifications about theoretical simplifications, non-universal unalignment and the need to test CHES more broadly.

D1.justification: Appendix I retains the same preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware and reproduction information, and code-link targets are unchanged. Correcting the Section 6.1 pointer adds no implementation information.

R1.justification: Cited works, references and research positioning in Section 7 and Appendix C are unchanged. Adding Yi Ren to the acknowledgements does not introduce a citation or revise the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: Section 6.1 corrects the reversed descriptions of Appendices H and I: H contains IPO experiments and I implementation details. v4 also acknowledges Yi Ren, adds punctuation in Appendix E.1 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, axes, legends and their placement are unchanged throughout both PDFs. The small text edits introduce no display redesign or page-layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: Correcting the reversed appendix descriptions in Section 6.1 provides a small editorial accuracy improvement by directing readers correctly to experiments and implementation details. The remaining edits are cosmetic or acknowledgements; scientific evidence, reasoning and reproducibility information are unchanged.
